texts.preamble: Da vs Afzal Ahmad on 22 March, 2018 In The Court Of Samar Vishal, Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate - Ii (New Delhi), Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cc No. 41455/2016 Date of Institution : 07.06.2005 Date of reserving judgement : 15.12.2017 Date of pronouncement : 22.03.2018 In re: Delhi Administration / Food Inspector Department of Pfa, Govt. of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area, Delhi-110035 ... Complainant versus Sh. Afzal Ahmad S/o Sh. Kalu Khan M/s Afzal Kiryana Store, B-343, Buland Masjid Shastri Park, Delhi - 53 ... Accused Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules. 2. As per the complaint, on 14.02.2005, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh R.K. Bhaskar and Field Assistant (herein after referred as FA) Sh Naubat Singh under the supervision of Local Health Authority (herein after referred to as DA vs Afzal Ahmad LHA)/SDM Sh Sameer C. Menz visited the premises of M/s Afzal Kiryana Store, B-343, Buland Masjid Shastri Park, Delhi - 53, where the accused Afzal Ahmad was found conducting the business of above mention shop, having stored food articles including "Mustard Oil" for human consumption. The Food Inspector disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of "Mustard Oil" from the vendor for analysis. The sample consisted of approx. 750 gms of Mustard Oil taken from an open tin container having no label declaration. The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. Sameer C. Menz, SDM/LHA. The sample of "Mustard Oil" was taken after proper mixing with the help of measure already lying in the tine container by rotating it in all possible directions. The Food Inspector divided the sample then and there into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles. Each sample bottle was separately packed, fastened and sealed according to Da vs Afzal Ahmad on 22 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25565441/ 1 PFA Act and Rules. The vendor's signatures were obtained on the LHA slip and the wrapper of the sample bottles. Notice in Form VI was given to accused Afzal Ahmad and the price of sample was also given to him vide vendor receipt dated 14.02.2005. Panchnama was prepared at the spot. All the documents prepared by F.l. were signed by accused Afzal Ahmad and the other witness FA Sh Naubat Singh. Before starting sample proceeding efforts were made to join public witnesses but none came forward, as such FA Sh.Naubat Singh was joined as witness. 3. One counter-part of the sample bearing LHA code No 52/LHA/10652 was also sent to Public Analyst, Delhi in intact DA vs Afzal Ahmad condition and remaining two counter-parts were deposited with the LHA in intact condition. Public Analyst analysed the sample and found the sample to be adulterated. The report of the Public Analyst is as follows: "The sample is adulterated because it is coloured with non permitted synthetic oil soluble coal tar dye. It also does not conform to standard with respect to BR, Saponification Value & un-saponifiable matter exceed the prescribed maximum limit of 60.5, 177 and 1.2% respectively and BTT is not within limit. The sample contains admixture of rice bran oil." It is further stated that the vendor was selling "Mustard Oil" in unpacked condition which is banned in Delhi vide notification No. F5(25)/98/PFA/Enf./5034 dated 27.08.98 issued by the Food (Health) Authority in pursuance of provisions of Clause (iv) of Section 7 of PFA Act, 1954. 4. It is the case of the complainant that accused Afzal Ahmad was the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Afzal Kiryana Store, B-343, Buland Masjid Shastri Park, Delhi - 53 at the time of sampling and he is incharge of and responsible for day to day conduct of the business of the said shop. 5. Thereafter on completion of investigation, sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA. The complaint was then filed in the court on 07.06.2005 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a)(b)(h)(j)(l)&(m) of PFA Act and Rule 23 read with Rule 28 & 29 & Rule 44 of PFA Rules, 1955 as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act against the accused. DA vs Afzal Ahmad 6. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 07.06.2005. The accused thereafter exercised their option of analysing the counter part through CFL under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act. The CFL reported that the sample did not confirm to standards as it was detected with non permitted synthetic oil and and saponification value exceeded the maximum limits. Based on the report of the CFL and pre charge evidence charge was framed against the accused for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1) (a) PFA Act being violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(b)(j)&(m) and Rule 28 & 29 of PFA Rules, 1955, to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Da vs Afzal Ahmad on 22 March, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25565441/ 2 7. At the trial, the prosecution examined four witness in support of its case i.e. PW-1 FI R.K. Bhaskar, PW-2 FA Naubat Singh, PW-3 S.C. Menz, PW-4 SDM/LHA Sh R.K. Chauhan. PW-1 FI R.K. Bhaskar, PW-2 FA Naubat Singh were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings under the supervision of SDM/LHA Sh Sh S.C. Menz. These witness narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of Mustard Oil approx. 750 gms from an open tin container bearing no identical label declaration and dividing it into three parts by putting in three clean and dry sample bottles, separately sealing, packing and marking the same and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses. They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's DA vs Afzal Ahmad receipt Ex.PW-1/A, Notice in Form VI Ex.PW-1/B and Panchnama Ex.PW-1/C. The vendor furnished his statement Ex.PW1/C2 at the spot and the notification banning the sale of loose mustard oil Ex.PW1/C1. Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample alongwith copy of memo in Form VII and another copy of memo in Form VII was deposited on th enext working day i.e. 15.02.2005 in intact condition with PA vide receipt Ex.PW1/D and two remaining counterparts of the sample in intact condition alongwith two copies of Memos in Form VII were deposited with LHA vide LHA receipt Ex.PW-1/E. Thereafter, PA Report Ex.PW-1/F was received, according to which the sample found adulterated because it was coloured with unpermitted synthetic oil soluble colouring matter. Thereafter PW-1 FI R.K. Bhaskar further investigated the matter and during investigation, he sent letter to STO, Ward No.75 and received its reply stating that no such firm was found registered with Sales Tax PW-1 FI R.K. Bhaskar also sent letter Ex.PW1/H to DHO, Naveen Shahadra Zone and received reply stating that no health license was issued to the accused. Thereafter, on completion of investigation, the entire case file was sent before the concerned SDM/LHA, who forwarded the same to the then Director PFA for obtaining his Consent and the then Director PFA Shri Diwan Chand granted his Consent for prosecution of accused persons after applying his mind vide Ex. PW1/I. Thereafter on the instruction of PW-4 SDM/LHA Sh R.K. Chauhan, the present complaint Ex.PW1/J was filed before the Court. Then intimation letter Ex.PW1/K alongwith copies of PA's Reports were sent to the accused persons through post vide postal receipt Ex.PW1/L. These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel. DA vs Afzal Ahmad 8. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC were recorded on 28.08.2015 wherein the accused denied the allegations and pleaded innocence. Thereafter the matter was fixed for defence evidence. 9. In defence evidence, the accused examined Sh S.N. Mehendru as DW-1. Thereafter, vide order dated 30.04.2016, the defence evidence was closed and the matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 13. In Calcutta Municipal Corporation v. Pawan Kumar Saraf [AIR DA vs Afzal Ahmad 1999 SC 738], it has been authoritatively laid down that the legal impact of a certificate of the Director of CFL is three fold: (a) it annuls or replaces the report of the PA, (b) it gains finality regarding the quality and standard of the food article involved in the case and (c) it becomes irrefutable so far as the facts stated therein are concerned. 14. In Subhash Chander v. State, Delhi Administration [1983(4) DRJ 100], it was observed by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "It has repeatedly been held by the supreme court that the certificate of the Director supersedes the report of the public analyst and is to be treated as conclusive evidence of its contents. The Director is a greater expert and therefore the statute says that his certificate shall be accepted by the court as conclusive evidence. In the landmark judgement titled as MCD v. Bishan Sarup [ILR 1970 (1) Delhi 518], the full bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi observed that "According to the scheme of the Act, the Director of Central Food Laboratory is constituted to be a sort of greater DA vs Afzal Ahmad expert than the Public Analyst and his certificate supersedes the report of Public Analyst under sub-section (3) of section 13". The Hon'ble Court also took a note of the ruling in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Ghisa Ram [AIR 1967 SC 970] wherein it was observed that the right has been given to the vendor for his satisfaction and proper defence, to get the sample analysed by a "greater expert whose certificate is to be accepted by court as conclusive evidence". Reliance can be placed on Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Zahiruddin [ILR (1972) 1 Del 630]. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Shriram Labhaya v. MCD [1948-1997 FAC DA vs Afzal Ahmad (SC) 483] has categorically held that testimony of the Food Inspector alone, if believed, is sufficient to convict the accused and there is no requirement of independent corroboration by public persons unless the testimony suffers from fatal inconsistencies. Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature, substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be. Section 2(ia)(b) it has to be established that the food article contains any other substance which injuriously affect the nature, substance or quality thereof.
